title: Geometric consequences of the Chow immersion
statement: Let m be a natural number, S, Z and X′ schemes [def-pc-scheme], g : Z → S and π : X′ → Z proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], and j : X′ → P^m_S an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] satisfying π ≫ g = j ≫ p_S, where p_S is the structure map [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Then j is a closed immersion, π ≫ g is projective [def-pc-projective-morphism], the induced map (j, π) : X′ → P^m_Z is a closed immersion, and π is projective.

proof.text: Composition gives properness of π ≫ g. Rewrite by hj and cancel the separated projective-space structure map using Mathlib IsProper.of_comp. The closed-range criterion IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion applied to j.isClosedMap.isClosed_range makes j closed. ProjectiveSpace.isClosedImmersion_liftBaseChange gives closedness of the induced map. The two displayed closed immersions and their factorization equalities witness IsHProjective; properness supplies QuasiCompact, giving IsProjective for both composites.

proof_origin.text: Lean proof using Mathlib proper cancellation and closed-range criterion, ProjectiveSpace base-change instance and the definition of IsProjective; follows the Chow paragraph of Stacks Tag 02O5.

lean.statement:
theorem chow_relative_ample_geometric (m : ℕ) (S Z X' : Scheme.{u})
    (g : Z ⟶ S) (π : X' ⟶ Z)
    (j : X' ⟶ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (m + 1)); S))
    [IsProper g] [IsProper π] [IsImmersion j]
    (hj : π ≫ g = j ≫ (ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (m + 1)); S) ↘ S)) :
    IsClosedImmersion j ∧ IsProjective (π ≫ g) ∧
      IsClosedImmersion (ProjectiveSpace.liftBaseChange π j hj) ∧ IsProjective π
